description:
Review finding from worktree-qzr2-wal-trim.

Problem:
Shale.Pushing owns predecessor ordering. A future push is parked until its predecessor arrives; when the gap closes, do_pending_pushes WAL-appends and acknowledges the queued successor internally. Shale.Server sees only the transaction handled by the current callback, so it forwards only that transaction to Demux. The drained successors are durable and acknowledged but absent from Demux, ShardServers, chunks, and materializer streams.

Observed reproduction:
Push version 2 before version 1. After version 1 closes the gap, the WAL reaches version 2 while the shard stream stops at version 1.

Correct model and invariants:
- Transaction delivery follows the sequencer predecessor chain {previous_version, commit_version}. Version gaps are valid; missing predecessor links are not.
- KCV is an independent, idempotent, monotonic watermark. It is accumulated with max and is not immutable per-transaction metadata.
- The client durability boundary remains WAL append plus fsync. Demux delivery is asynchronous and reconstructible from the WAL; ACKs must not wait for Demux.
- Shale passes each original encoded transaction binary to Demux unchanged. Demux remains the sole mutation slicer; no per-shard slicing or binary copying belongs in Shale.

Required change:
1. Make Pushing expose every transaction successfully appended by one push/drain operation. Return the original encoded binaries in predecessor-chain order. Any error result after partial progress must retain the last valid State and the successfully appended prefix so those appends cannot become invisible.
2. Have Shale.Server forward every returned binary once, in order, using the commit version encoded in that transaction. The guarantee is one forwarding event per WAL append within a live Demux incarnation; recovery intentionally replays into a fresh incarnation.
3. Decouple queued KCV handling from transaction delivery. A valid KCV that is strictly newer than Demuxs held value advances it with max even when the associated transaction is parked. This advancement must not change Demux high_water; it may re-evaluate an already-pending cut. Immediately appended transactions keep the existing piggyback path. When a queued transaction later drains, Demuxs held maximum is propagated through the normal shard/currency path.
4. Preserve the existing WAL ACK boundary and the existing ownership split: Pushing schedules/appends, Server forwards, and Demux slices.

Why KCV-only advancement is safe:
Every required Bedrock log receives a transaction at every assigned version, including empty transactions, and the sequencer advances KCV only after a commit is durable on every required log. Therefore a valid KCV observed by a running log cannot be ahead of that logs durable predecessor prefix. Messages from one Shale process to its Demux are ordered, so earlier transaction forwards are processed before a later standalone KCV advancement.

Impact:
Without the fix, acknowledged writes can disappear from the read path and object-storage durability. WAL trimming can make the omission permanent. Replicas that receive the same pushes in different arrival orders can also construct different chunk contents.

Acceptance criteria:
- Pushing returns every successfully WAL-appended transaction in predecessor-chain order, including the successful prefix when a later drain entry fails.
- Server forwards each returned transaction binary unchanged and exactly once per live-incarnation append event.
- A future queued push with a greater KCV advances the Demux KCV monotonically without advancing transaction high_water; no pending entry is required to retain its original KCV.
- Concurrent shuffled pushes leave WAL last_version, Demux high_water, ShardServer contents, and materializer-visible state at the same final version.
- A regression test uses the real Shale.Server and a real or instrumented Demux, not ACK-only assertions.
- Replica tests use different arrival orders and verify identical ordered shard slices and deterministic chunk payloads.
- Relevant log/Shale guides are updated to describe queued future predecessor links and the separation between transaction ordering and KCV.

Non-goals:
- Per-entry WAL backpressure and rejection while draining remain bedrock-qzr.23.
- KCV-only wakeups through the materializer currency protocol are a separate two-dimensional currency concern; this ticket only ensures the watermark is retained at Demux and propagated by the next normal transaction/currency event.
- Log long-pull notification changes are not part of this bug; Log.pull is recovery-only.
title: Forward every queued out-of-order Shale push through Demux
